Cp — potential process capability, short-term. Compares specification width to short-term (within-subgroup) spread; does not account for centering.
Cpk — actual process capability, short-term. Like Cp, but accounts for how centred the process is between the limits.
Pp — potential process capability, long-term. Uses the overall population standard deviation rather than a short-term estimate.
Ppk — actual process capability, long-term. Uses the overall population standard deviation and accounts for centering.

Nelson Rule 4: flags 14 consecutive points, ending at CurrentOrder, that alternate up/down throughout.

itens.descricao: Financial functions for project's profitability calculation

funcoes.sobre: Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) is a valuation method that estimates the value of an investment, for each period of the project, based on its expected future cash flows (Cash Flow = Revenue + Costs + Investment), discounted using a discount factor. Put Costs and Investment in negative value. The Discounted Rate is a decimal value representing a percentage. For example, 0.101 for 10.1%.

Discount Factor (DF) is a valuation method that estimates, for each period of the project, the value of one euro adjusted for inflation or to a minimum expected return on the investment, this the "Discount Rate". The Discounted Rate is a decimal value representing a percentage. For example, 0.101 for 10.1%. Note: Entering the value of an investment helps determine the first year of the project.

Free Cash Flow (FCF) is a valuation method that estimates the value of an investment, for each period of the project, based on its expected future cash flows (Cash Flow = Revenue + Costs + Investment), discounted using a discount factor. Put Costs and Investment in negative value. The Discounted Rate is a decimal value representing a percentage. For example, 0.101 for 10.1%.

Internal Rate of Return (IRR). The IRR is the discount rate at wich the net present value (NPV) of a set of Discounted Cash Flows (DCF) is eaqual to zero. Put Costs and Investment in negative value. The Discounted Rate is a decimal value representing a percentage. For example, 0.101.  for 10.1%. "Fact_table" is the business data table.

Net Present Value (NPV). This is the cumulative Discounted Cash Flow (DCF), for each period of the project. NPV evaluates the profitability of an investment by comparing the present value of expected future cash flows to the initial investment. Put Costs and Investment in negative value. The Discounted Rate is a decimal value representing a percentage. For example, 0.101 for 10.1%.
Net Present Value (NPV). This is the value of the NPV for the entire project. Useful for KPI.
Payback Number Year determines the number of years required to achieve a return on investment, so when the NPV becomes positive.
"Payback Year" determines the year of return on investment, that is, the moment when the NPV becomes positive.

Asserts that a column contains at least one non-NULL value (not DAX BLANK()). It does not check that no row is NULL; for that, use NullCountShouldBeAtMost(testName, tableRef, columnRef, 0).

Asserts that every value in a column is NULL (BLANK()) or an empty string (""). Deprecated: this is a duplicate of ShouldBeNullOrBlank (same logic and results), and its name suggests empty strings only. Use ShouldBeNullOrBlank.

Asserts that no value in a column is NULL (BLANK()) or an empty string (""). Deprecated: this is a duplicate of ShouldNotBeNullOrBlank (same logic and results), and its name suggests empty strings only. Use ShouldNotBeNullOrBlank, or BlankRateShouldBeAtMostV2(testName, tableRef, columnRef, 0) to check for empty strings only.

Asserts that all values in a column are not NULL and not BLANK. Fails if any NULL or empty values exist.

Asserts that a column exists in a table.
Presence / Completeness Thresholds

Asserts that the blank rate (empty string) of a column is at most the specified percentage. Deprecated: use BlankRateShouldBeAtMostV2. Divides by the number of distinct values, not rows, so the reported rate is wrong for any column with repeated values.

Asserts that the null or blank rate of a column is at most the specified percentage. Deprecated: use NullOrBlankRateShouldBeAtMostV2. Divides by the number of distinct values, not rows, so the reported rate is wrong for any column with repeated values.

Asserts that the populated (non-null, non-blank) rate of a column is at least the specified percentage. Deprecated: use PopulatedRateShouldBeAtLeastV2. Divides by the number of distinct values, not rows, so the reported rate is wrong for any column with repeated values.

Asserts that a column has at most maxCount NULL (BLANK()) rows. Pass 0 to require that no row is NULL. Empty strings ("") are not NULL; use BlankRateShouldBeAtMostV2 or NullOrBlankRateShouldBeAtMostV2 for those.

Asserts that the share of NULL (BLANK()) rows in a column is at most maxNullPct percent (0-100). Counts rows of tableRef, unlike NullRateShouldBeAtMost, which divides by distinct values. Empty strings ("") are not NULL. Fails with NO ROWS when tableRef is empty.

Asserts that the share of empty-string ("") rows in a column is at most maxBlankPct percent (0-100). NULL (BLANK()) rows are not counted. Counts rows of tableRef, unlike BlankRateShouldBeAtMost, which divides by distinct values. Works on columns of any data type. Fails with NO ROWS when tableRef is empty.

Asserts that the share of NULL (BLANK()) or empty-string ("") rows in a column is at most maxPct percent (0-100). Counts rows of tableRef, unlike NullOrBlankRateShouldBeAtMost, which divides by distinct values. Fails with NO ROWS when tableRef is empty.

Asserts that the share of populated (not NULL and not "") rows in a column is at least minPct percent (0-100). Counts rows of tableRef, unlike PopulatedRateShouldBeAtLeast, which divides by distinct values. Fails with NO ROWS when tableRef is empty.

Asserts that the combination of two columns forms a distinct composite key. Fails with NO VALUES when the column has no non-NULL value. (Changed in 0.8.0: 0.7.x could pass a column with no values.)

Asserts that a column contains no duplicate values. Alias for ShouldBeDistinct. Deprecated: use NonNullValuesShouldBeDistinct (blanks ignored) or ShouldBePrimaryKey (blanks fail). Compares DISTINCTCOUNT, which counts BLANK as a value, with COUNTA, which ignores it: one BLANK fails an otherwise distinct column, and {1, 1, BLANK} passes.

Asserts that the non-NULL values in a column are all distinct. NULL (BLANK()) rows are ignored; empty strings ("") count as values. Use ShouldBePrimaryKey to also forbid NULL and empty values. Fails with NO VALUES when the column has no non-NULL value.
Asserts that a column can serve as a primary key: no NULL (BLANK()) or empty-string ("") rows, and all values distinct.

Asserts that a column has at most maxCount duplicate values among its non-NULL rows (non-NULL rows minus distinct non-NULL values). NULL (BLANK()) rows are ignored. Fails with NO VALUES when the column has no non-NULL value.

Asserts that the maximum value in a column is at most the specified value. Fails with NO VALUES when the column has no non-NULL value. (Changed in 0.8.0: 0.7.x could pass a column with no values.)

Asserts that a table has exactly the expected number of rows.

Schema & Column Shape
Asserts that a table does not have extra columns beyond the allowed list (comma-separated).
Asserts that a column in a table has the expected data type.

Asserts that every row of a key table is distinct, for composite keys of any width. Pass the key columns as a projection, e.g. SELECTCOLUMNS('Sales', "OrderID", 'Sales'[OrderID], "Line", 'Sales'[Line]). Blank key values are compared like any other value. Fails with NO ROWS when keyTable is empty.

Asserts that a filtered table has at most maxCount rows. Pass the rows that break a rule, e.g. FILTER('Orders', NOT 'Orders'[Status] IN {"open", "closed"}). Zero matching rows passes, including on an empty table.
Asserts that a filtered table's rows are at most maxPct percent (0-100) of a base table's rows. Fails with NO ROWS when baseTable is empty.
